items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I always played the first trombone with Louie and I would take charge of the trombone section

ctx.x: I see. Okay. Let's see you made some recordings later in the year with the Louie Armstrong orchestra and noting from the discography there was a change in personnel, especially in the trumpet section and in the trombone section. There's always changes in personnel but it seems that the trumpet and trombone people this time were the ones that were replaced or left the orchestra for one reason or another, while the reed section stayed intact. Joe Garland was in that. Don Hill, John Sparrow and Amos Gordon Ernest…

Well, at different times when a man would come in from a tour back in New York, invariably some of the brass men, I don't know how it turned out that way -- would leave. Maybe they couldn't stand the road or anything like that. I always played the first trombone with Louie and I would take charge of the trombone section and different guys would come in andout, I guess they were tired of the road --

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: he had Lips Page on trumpet, Big Chief on trombone

ctx.x: It's amazing, I think, for us, especially those of us who have not traveled extensively, it's hard for us to realize that jazz has made this tremendous inroad. And it's gone into every country.

It's, listen, man, it's something that nobody can change. I'll tell you why. when Bechet was in Paris playing at a jazz festival one time, Charlie Parker was living there and he was on that bill. So they're going to give Paris something new. But they still got the good old timers there in case something go wrong and good thing they had him. Charlie Parker wouldn't even speak to Bechet coming up or going over on the plane because he's, you know, just going to be here. But Bechet ain't worried about him because he…
What about some of the, some of the far out musicians, Louie? Are they saying anything with their music? Are they, are they really talking?
